title: The First Computer 'Bug' Was an Actual Bug
description:
Before "bug" meant a software glitch, it meant an actual insect stuck in a computer. Here's the real 1947 story, and the logbook page that's still around to prove it.

#shorts #techfacts #computerhistory

scenes.text: The first ever computer bug was a literal moth, stuck inside a room-sized machine at Harvard in 1947.
The Harvard Mark II kept failing, and nobody could figure out why -- until the team opened it up.
They found the moth trapped between the relay contacts, jamming the circuit.
They taped the moth into the logbook with the note, quote, first actual case of bug being found.
The term 'bug' for a technical glitch already existed before this, going back to Thomas Edison. But this moment is why 'debugging' stuck.
That logbook page still exists today, in the Smithsonian's collection -- a real moth, taped down, that gave programming its favorite word.
Did you know 'debugging' came from an actual bug before today?
